To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression system of co-expressing EglII and bglZ in B. megaterium MS94 is the best choice to generate enzymes for hydrolysis of sugarcane baggasse.

a combination of endo/exo-glucanase and GH 1 β-glucoside hydrolases are required for hydrolysis of crystalline cellulose, and that the combination enzymes can act on pretreated biomass more efficiently.
a combination of endo-glucanase and exo-glucosidases from Bacillus amiloliquefaciens was expressed in Bacillus megatarium and used to hydrolyze crystalline cellulose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
construction of EglII, BglZ and their combinations, which can be applied to convert sugarcane bagassse to sugars for further fermentation to bioethanol.
the construction and characterization of the cellulase enzymes for hydrolysis of biomass.
the construction of individual, fused and co-expressed enzymes, and their catalytic efficiency for hydrolyzing biomass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
co-expression of EglII+BglII is the best choice for producing enzymes for hydrolysis of biomass, and the enzymes can be used for hydrolyzing biomass in the form of either individual or fused protein.
a combination of endo/exoglucanase, and a combination of β-glucoside and β-glucuronidase are required for the complete hydrolysis of cellulose and hemicellulose, respectively.
the expression system of coex-bglz+eglII is the best choice to construct enzymes for hydrolysis of sugarcane baggas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the co-expressed protein of EglII with BglZ was the best choice for producing enzymes for hydrolysis of sugarcane baggas.
a combination of EglIIBglZ was required for converting sugarcane bagassse to sugars.
the enzymes of GH 1 and GH 5 families could work together in a synergistic manner to hydrolyzing crystallin cellulose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the co-expression system of EglII (exoglucanase/endoglucanase) and BglZ (β-glucosidases) is a better option to produce enzymes for converting sugarcane bagassse to fermentable sugars.
co-expressing EglII and β-glucosiadse in the same strain is a promising approach for biomass conversion.
the combination of endoglulcanase and β-glusosidase can be used to hydrolyze crystalline cellulose, which has potential for converting lignocellulose biomass to fermentable sugars.
